tema: Analyses the differential expression of mitochondrial proteins in CFS through proteomics, starting from discordant monozygotic twins.
diseno: Bottom-up proteomics (nano-LC-MS) of platelet mitochondria in a pair of discordant twins; validation by Western blot in saliva from 45 CFS patients and 45 controls, with stratification by clinical parameters.
hallazgos: Overexpression of ATPB and ACON in CFS was confirmed, but not the alteration of MDHM. Values were higher in patients with clinical features similar to the ill twin; ATPB and MDHM correlated with IFN-γ and TNF-α, and ACON negatively with IL-2.
conclusion: These proteins could be a supporting diagnostic criterion and, rather than for a universal diagnosis, would serve to characterize subgroups and guide personalized treatments.
triangulacion: Coherence among the three sources. The conclusions (from the discussion) add the correlations with cytokines and qualify the universal diagnostic usefulness because of the heterogeneity of CFS.

tema: Reviews the differentiation between psychosomatic, somatopsychic and multisystem diseases and medical uncertainty, to reduce misdiagnosis.
diseno: Narrative review with two illustrative clinical cases and terminological discussion.
hallazgos: Rare, complex and multisystem diseases are frequently misdiagnosed. Terms such as medically unexplained symptoms or somatoform disorder are obsolete; several psychogenic diagnoses may be overdiagnosed; bodily distress lacks scientific support.
conclusion: A psychiatric diagnosis cannot be based solely on the absence of findings; complete clinical evaluation, humility and better training at the medicine-psychiatry interface will improve diagnostic accuracy and trust.
triangulacion: High coherence between sources. The PDF conclusions explicitly cite Lyme and ME/CFS as examples of diseases mislabelled as psychogenic, a focus that the keywords (centred on psychiatric terminology) do not capture.

tema: Compares the functional status and wellbeing of people with ME/CFS versus people with multiple sclerosis and healthy controls.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with data from the UK ME/CFS Biobank; SF-36v2 and an ad hoc questionnaire on employment and income. Sample size not stated in the abstract.
hallazgos: People with ME/CFS scored significantly worse in almost all SF-36v2 domains, especially the physical component, role physical and social function; the smallest difference was in mental health. They work fewer hours and have lower incomes.
conclusion: People with ME/CFS are measurably more disabled than people with MS; this should motivate recognition, advocacy for their needs and better research funding.
triangulacion: High coherence. The PDF conclusions add social isolation, job loss and the need to validate with larger samples, a nuance of caution absent from the abstract.

tema: Participatory research (Chronic Illness Inclusion Project) on disability identity and discrimination in chronic illness, proposing the concept of 'energy impairment'.
diseno: Asynchronous online qualitative forum with 20 participants over eight weeks and a validation survey with 2300 responses; emancipatory disability research tradition.
hallazgos: Participants experience physical and cognitive energy limitation, and systemic invalidation and disbelief that acts as discrimination (disablism), affecting identity, self-esteem and access to support. The terms 'energy-limiting chronic illness' and 'energy impairment' received the highest approval; 34% of the UK disabled population report energy impairment.
conclusion: There is an incipient advocacy movement based on shared bodily experiences; governments should incorporate energy impairment into data collection and disability policy.
triangulacion: The keywords (inclusion, ableism, disability policy) agree with the abstract and conclusions; the latter add that the term does not fit all symptom profiles, a nuance of caution. It does not focus specifically on ME/CFS.

tema: Evaluates whether erythrocyte deformability is reduced in ME/CFS as a possible biomarker.
diseno: Case-control study with 9 pairs of ME/CFS patients and age- and sex-matched controls; high-throughput microfluidic device that mimics microcapillaries, recording at 4000 fps and image analysis of entry time, transit velocity and elongation index, together with biochemical techniques.
hallazgos: Patients' erythrocytes had a longer entry time (~12%), lower mean transit velocity (~17%) and lower elongation index (~14%), all with p<0.0001.
conclusion: The data show that erythrocytes from ME/CFS patients have reduced deformability; the rest of the conclusions are not available because the abstract is truncated.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent on erythrocyte deformability, microvascular flow and oxidative stress; no conclusions are available and the abstract is cut off before the corroborating measurements, so triangulation is incomplete.

tema: Investigates whether daily fluctuations of cytokines, especially leptin, are associated with daily fatigue severity in CFS.
diseno: Longitudinal study with 10 women with CFS (Fukuda criteria) and 10 controls matched for age and BMI; 25 consecutive days of blood draws and self-reported symptoms; Luminex panel of 51 cytokines (500 samples) and post hoc machine learning algorithm.
hallazgos: Daily fatigue correlated significantly with leptin in 6 CFS participants and in 1 control. The algorithm distinguished days of high and low fatigue in the CFS group with an accuracy of 78.3%.
conclusion: The results support a role of cytokines in the pathophysiology of CFS and identify a subgroup with a strong correlation between leptin and fatigue; these approaches could reveal biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions (with table and figure noise) qualify that the association with leptin occurs in a subgroup, not in all patients, and the sample is small.

tema: Critically reviews the enteroviral theory of ME/CFS aetiology and the methodologies used to detect persistent enteroviral infections.
diseno: Critical literature review with in silico evaluation of published primers. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Previous research supports a higher prevalence of chronic enteroviral infections in ME/CFS cohorts, but inconsistent results reduced interest; the methods used were inadequate to rule out chronic infection.
conclusion: There is considerable evidence that previous ME/CFS outbreaks were caused by enteroviruses, and studies with adequate samples and techniques such as optimized RT-PCR or RNAseq with targeted capture are urgently needed.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion are consistent; the discussion specifies the methodological recommendations (detection of positive and negative strands, targeted RNAseq) and contains noise from contributions and funding.

tema: Investigates whether a defect in mitochondrial ATP synthesis explains fatigue and poorer performance on repeated exercise in CFS/ME.
diseno: Case-control study with 15 women with CFS/ME and 15 controls; two CPETs 24 h apart, oxidative phosphorylation (complexes I and II) in permeabilized PBMC and plasma CK.
hallazgos: Patients reached the anaerobic threshold and maximal effort with lower oxygen consumption, worsening on the second test. Oxidative phosphorylation in PBMC and plasma CK were similar between groups.
conclusion: The lower ATP synthesis is not due to a defect of the oxidative phosphorylation complexes but to another factor; the authors conclude that oxygen transport capacity is limited.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions go beyond the abstract in attributing the deficit to limited oxygen transport, and acknowledge the reduced sample size.

tema: Evaluates the functional status and wellbeing of people with ME/CFS and their caregivers, comparing them with other chronic diseases.
diseno: Cross-sectional study; 170 people aged 18-64 with well-characterized ME/CFS and 44 caregivers; SF-36 v2 compared with population norms and 10 chronic diseases.
hallazgos: Very reduced scores in ME/CFS, especially physical (mean PCS 26.8; MCS 34.1); the lowest was Role physical (25.4). Values lower than the general population and other diseases; caregivers showed low scores in the mental domain (45.4).
conclusion: ME/CFS is disabling, with a greater impact than other chronic diseases such as cancer, and its emotional burden reaches caregivers; SF-36 is recommended alongside objective measures.
triangulacion: High coherence among the three sources. The PDF conclusions stress the difficulty of assessing a barely visible disability and its usefulness for planning services; they include abbreviation noise.

tema: Autobiographical essay on how pathologizing labels in psychotherapy can constitute gaslighting and harm clients.
diseno: Testimonial narrative by the author with theoretical reflection (social constructionism); no sample.
hallazgos: Describes how a psychology professor and a psychotherapist gaslit her through pathologizing labels, generating double binds and betrayal during her recovery from interpersonal abuse.
conclusion: To reduce the risk of gaslighting, therapists must affirm the client's strengths and avoid undermining their perspective; proposes reforming or eliminating the use of pathologizing labels.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent around gaslighting and diagnostic labels; the conclusions (from the discussion) add client feedback systems and include acknowledgement noise. It does not mention ME/CFS.

tema: Evaluates whether ME/CFS patients reproduce peak VO2 and other parameters on a second CPET at 24 h and the implications for functional assessment.
diseno: Study with 22 ME/CFS patients and two CPETs 24 h apart; VO2, HR, ventilation, workload and RER at peak and ventilatory threshold; ANOVA and Wilcoxon.
hallazgos: Significant decreases on CPET2: peak VO2 13.8%, peak HR 9 bpm, peak ventilation 14.7%, peak workload 12.5%; at the ventilatory threshold VO2 15.8%, ventilation 7.4% and workload 21.3%. RER did not change. With a single CPET, functional capacity was overestimated by 50%.
conclusion: Patients do not reproduce most measures on the second CPET; repeated CPET deserves consideration as a clinical indicator and classification with a single test underestimates disability.
triangulacion: The three sources agree. The conclusions add that the protocol can guide exertion guidelines to avoid exacerbations, in line with the activity prescription keyword.

tema: Tests the hypothesis that hypermobility, signs of intracranial hypertension (IH) and craniocervical obstructions are over-represented in ME/CFS and explain many symptoms.
diseno: Retrospective cross-sectional study at a specialist clinic; 229 patients with severe ME/CFS (Canadian criteria; 190 women and 39 men); Beighton score, optic nerve sheath diameter/eyeball ratio on brain MRI, position of the cerebellar tonsils, cervical MRI and quantitative sensory testing.
hallazgos: 50% had hypermobility; of 205 with brain MRI, 55% had increased ONSD and 83% signs of possible IH (32% severe); 56% had cerebellar tonsils below the McRae line. Of 125 with cervical MRI, 80% had craniocervical obstructions; 96% had allodynia and 76% fibromyalgia.
conclusion: There is a large over-representation of hypermobility, signs of IH and craniocervical obstructions compared with the general population, which could explain symptoms such as brain fog, orthostatic intolerance and PEM; if confirmed, a diagnostic and therapeutic paradigm shift would be possible.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions are more ambitious than the abstract in attributing neuroinflammation and autoimmunity to these signs, without the comparison with the general population being based on a control group of their own.

tema: Measures plasma cytokines, chemokines and growth factors in long-standing ME/CFS patients compared with controls.
diseno: Case-control study with 100 patients with long-duration chronic ME/CFS and 79 controls matched for sex and age; plasma measurement of 34 analytes and multivariate cluster analysis; comparison with infectious and autoimmune liver diseases.
hallazgos: Highly significant reductions of IL-16, IL-7 and VEGF-A were observed, correlated with each other in the cluster analysis, in addition to decreases of fractalkine (CX3CL1) and MIG (CXCL9) and an increase of eotaxin 2 (CCL24). The profile was not observed in liver diseases with persistent fatigue.
conclusion: The clustered reduction of IL-7, IL-16 and VEGF-A could have physiological and specific relevance in ME/CFS and, if confirmed in other cohorts, open new diagnostic and therapeutic avenues.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the discussion, with noise from acknowledgements and funding) are consistent on IL-16, IL-7 and VEGF-A; the conclusions also stress analytical rigour (LLOD, LLOQ, CV) as a possible explanation for discrepancies in the literature.

tema: ME Association A-Z index of the most relevant published research on ME/CFS (August 2021).
diseno: Reference compilation document organized by topic; no own study. Text available only as opening text.
hallazgos: Collects key studies and documents on ME/CFS ordered by the headings of the MEA clinical and research guide, updated monthly.
conclusion: Not stated.
triangulacion: Only the opening text (foreword) is available; there are no keywords or conclusions, so triangulation is not possible.

tema: Evaluates the biochemical changes associated with self-reported severity of post-exertional malaise (PEM) in ME/CFS.
diseno: Observational study with 47 ME/CFS cases and matched controls; clinical examination, questionnaires, serum biochemistry and serum and urine metabolomics; 35 of 46 cases with PEM in the last 7 days formed the PEM group.
hallazgos: The main change was a decrease in hypoxanthine, correlated with alterations of the glucose:lactate ratio suggesting a glycolytic abnormality. Urinary excretion of methylhistidine, mannitol and acetate increased, indicating a hypermetabolic event.
conclusion: PEM is associated with changes in glycolysis and acetylation compatible with a hypoacetylation state that could alter histone acetylation; well-designed studies are required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on hypermetabolism, purines and hypoacetylation. The conclusions are more cautious than the abstract, which attributes the primary events of PEM to hypoacetylation.

tema: Compares the response to a two-day CPET in women with severe ME/CFS versus mild and moderate forms.
diseno: Study with 82 women with ME/CFS (31 mild, 31 moderate, 20 severe according to the International Consensus Criteria); VO2, HR and workload at peak and ventilatory threshold.
hallazgos: In all severity groups the parameters fell significantly from day 1 to 2; the magnitude was similar except for peak workload, whose decrease was greater in the severe group (-19%) compared with the mild.
conclusion: The reductions on the second day are confirmed and it is shown for the first time that severity negatively influences exercise capacity, with the greatest deterioration in peak workload in the severe group.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions reproduce the abstract without new nuances.

tema: Tests the hypothesis that fatigue in ME/CFS is due in part to defects in cellular energy supply, using the ATP Profile test.
diseno: Audit of 138 ME/CFS patients (18-65 years) from a private practice and 53 healthy controls; ATP Profile in neutrophils and circulating cell-free DNA in plasma; comparison with a previous cohort of 61 patients.
hallazgos: All patients showed measurable mitochondrial dysfunction correlated with severity, with two groups according to metabolic compensation. Cell-free DNA indicated tissue damage up to 3.5 times the normal range, correlated with the dysfunction; the immediate causes would be lack of substrates and partial blockade of the translocase.
conclusion: The ATP Profile would be a valuable diagnostic tool; ME/CFS is a serious disease that could affect all cells of the body.
triangulacion: There are no keywords. Abstract and conclusions (from the discussion, with noise from figures and correspondence) are consistent; the conclusions are broader and defer treatment to future work.

tema: Reviews the immuno-inflammatory and oxidative and nitrosative stress (O&NS) pathways that could explain mitochondrial dysfunction in ME/CFS.
diseno: Narrative literature review. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1, TNF-α), elastase and O&NS can inhibit mitochondrial respiration, the electron transport chain and ATP production, and damage mtDNA and membranes; low levels of antioxidants, zinc, CoQ10 and omega-3 fatty acids would aggravate the process.
conclusion: Immuno-inflammatory and O&NS pathways would probably be the drivers of mitochondrial dysfunction, generating a spiral of energy decline that could explain fatigue, PEM and brain alterations.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent. The conclusions are more assertive (probable drivers, spiral) than the conditional formulation of the abstract.

tema: Investigates the existence of neuroinflammation in ME/CFS using 11C-(R)-PK11195 PET.
diseno: 11C-(R)-PK11195 PET (TSPO ligand) in 9 patients and 10 healthy controls; cerebellum as reference region; questionnaires on fatigue, cognition, pain and depression.
hallazgos: Binding potential was 45-199% higher in the cingulate, hippocampus, amygdala, thalamus, midbrain and pons. It correlated with cognitive impairment (amygdala, thalamus, midbrain), pain (cingulate, thalamus) and depression (hippocampus).
conclusion: Neuroinflammation is present in extensive areas and is associated with the severity of neuropsychological symptoms; PET could help objective diagnosis and anti-inflammatory strategies.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on neuroinflammation, TSPO and microglia/astrocytes; the conclusions broaden the clinical usefulness of PET despite the small sample.

tema: Presents news on the role of comorbidity and emerging treatments in ME/CFS, centred on immune, inflammatory and metabolic processes.
diseno: Review and opinion article based on clinical experience and literature, with imaging examples (NeuroSPECT); no sample size stated.
hallazgos: Promising results are reported with metformin or Momordica charantia extract to correct insulin resistance, meldonium for mitochondrial glucose transport, sodium dichloroacetate to activate pyruvate dehydrogenase and nutraceutical supplements; antibiotics and antivirals have not proven effective.
conclusion: ME/CFS should be considered an orphan disease; optimizing glucose metabolism has been effective in some cases and these combinations deserve further research, together with treatment of comorbidity.
triangulacion: Keywords (metformin, insulin resistance, meldonium) and abstract agree; the discussion adds the lack of efficacy of antibiotics and antivirals and includes noise from legends and acknowledgements. The evidence is mainly clinical and uncontrolled.

tema: Retrospectively evaluates the off-label use of low-dose aripiprazole as a treatment for ME/CFS.
diseno: Retrospective study (letter to the editor) of 101 patients treated with low-dose aripiprazole at Stanford; detailed methods not stated in the available text.
hallazgos: According to the discussion, some patients did not obtain benefit and a small subgroup had adverse effects that required discontinuing the drug; overall the results suggest symptom reduction.
conclusion: Aripiprazole could effectively reduce ME/CFS symptoms and deserves a randomized clinical trial; studying its mechanism in neuroinflammatory conditions could contribute to understanding pathogenesis.
triangulacion: The abstract is actually header and licence, with no content; the conclusions (discussion, with noise from acknowledgements and affiliations) agree with the keywords and title, although they are cautious in calling for an RCT.

tema: Describes the onset patterns and course of ME/CFS in a US cohort.
diseno: Descriptive study with a detailed survey of 150 people meeting the 1994 Fukuda criteria; descriptive statistics.
hallazgos: Peri-onset events: infections (64%), stress (39%) and environmental toxins (20%). The main symptoms persist but diminish; cognitive ones change less. 47% could not work, 59% described a fluctuating course, 97% had comorbidities and 13% a first-degree family history.
conclusion: Offers a broad epidemiological view that confirms previous studies and highlights little-examined aspects, such as the evolution of symptoms and the role of the female reproductive cycle.
triangulacion: High coherence among the three sources. The PDF conclusions go beyond the abstract in proposing hypotheses about the stress response, autonomic and autoimmune systems, and future studies with biomarkers and HLA.

tema: Opinion article that applies what has been learned in ME/CFS to long COVID and proposes a unifying hypothesis of both conditions.
diseno: Opinion article based on literature and clinical experience. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Highlights PEM as a distinctive symptom and oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction as underlying pathophysiologies; proposes grouping ME/CFS and long COVID as post-active phase of infection syndromes (PAPIS), with similar biochemical pathways regardless of the trigger.
conclusion: For many symptoms long COVID is ME/CFS, although the two are not synonymous; investigating PAPIS could lead to therapies, and failing to address it will have serious socioeconomic and clinical consequences.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion are consistent with the unifying hypothesis; the discussion qualifies that long COVID includes symptoms outside ME/CFS and is not synonymous with it.

tema: Examines the efficacy of pain inhibitory systems during two types of exercise in ME/CFS and their relationship to PEM.
diseno: Controlled experimental study with 22 women with ME/CFS and 22 sedentary controls; submaximal exercise and physiologically limited self-paced exercise; pressure pain thresholds, questionnaires and accelerometry.
hallazgos: In ME/CFS, pain thresholds decreased after both exercises, whereas they increased in healthy women, with symptom worsening; the reduction after the submaximal exercise was associated with post-exertional fatigue (r=0.454).
conclusion: There is abnormal central pain processing during exercise and both submaximal and self-paced exercise trigger PEM; modalities and intensities that do not exacerbate symptoms must be identified.
triangulacion: The conclusions come from the abstract itself and agree with it and with the keywords (pain inhibition, central processing). There is no independent source of conclusions.

tema: Reviews the pathological mechanisms underlying ME/CFS across multiple body systems.
diseno: Narrative literature review. No sample stated.
hallazgos: The evidence shows immune and inflammatory alterations, autonomic and neurological dysfunction, muscle and mitochondrial abnormalities, metabolic changes and intestinal or microbiota alterations, possibly intertwined in a broad homeostatic shift.
conclusion: ME/CFS is heterogeneous and could reflect alternative stable homeostatic states; it is a priority to develop phenotyping and stratification tools and to carry out experimental cause-effect studies rather than correlational ones.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions are more critical than the abstract in stressing that research has been based on correlations and that causal relationships cannot be established with confidence.
